license_note: Dash-size dimensions and tolerances are the published values of SAE Aerospace Standard AS568 (current revision AS568D, 2014; earlier revisions carry the same nominal numbers), owned by SAE International; dimensions are facts and are reproduced verbatim in every O-ring vendor catalogue. They were not read from the SAE document in this session: the compiler wrote them from catalogue memory and the reconciliation cross-checked all 299 rows against two independently published open-source AS568 tables (the Apple Rubber AS568 quick-reference chart as transcribed in v2gundam/o-ring-fit, and KasperCalc oring-sizes.js citing SAE AS568D) and the per-dash rows of the Parker Table 4-2 transcription in KasperCalc; every id_in, cs_in and W tolerance agrees across all three after the -151 correction, and the ID tolerances agree between the two sources that carry them except -225, -469, -470. "likely" therefore means: matches three independent published tables and the compiler's catalogue memory; "recall" marks the rows a reviewer or a source disputed; no row is "certain" because none was read from the standard itself. Gland design values (supplement.gland_parker_ord5700, parker_t42_* columns) are Parker Hannifin's published recommendations from the Parker O-Ring Handbook ORD 5700 (Design Chart 4-1, Table 4-2, Chart 4-3, Figure 3-2), cited as such; values marked "recall" there were not verified against a transcription. Selection practice marked "PartForge doctrine" is club shop practice, not Parker.

columns.id_in: nominal inside diameter, inches, as AS568 tabulates it (JSON number; use id_in_str for the exact printed text)
columns.id_in_str: id_in exactly as the standard prints it, 3 decimals, string
columns.id_mm: id_in x 25.4 to 3 decimals (the AS568D metric column rounds to 2, e.g. -240 = 94.84)
columns.id_tol_in: ID tolerance +/- inches, per dash, from the Apple Rubber AS568 chart (cross-checked vs the Parker Table 4-2 transcription; the larger is carried where they differ, see disputed)
columns.cs_in: nominal cross-section W, inches (series constant .103/.139/.210/.275 - a fixed standard value; row confidence refers to id_in and id_tol_in)
columns.cs_in_str: cs_in exactly as the standard prints it, 3 decimals, string (".210", not 0.21)
columns.cs_mm_std: cross-section as the AS568D metric column and Parker print it, 2 decimals (2.62 / 3.53 / 5.33 / 6.99) - use this in drawings and hints
columns.od_in: nominal outside diameter = id_in + 2 x cs_in, inches (derived, not an AS568 column, NOT a groove diameter)
columns.parker_t42_in: Parker ORD 5700 Design Table 4-2 gland diameters for this dash, inches: A_bore (bore, male/piston gland, +.002/-0), B1_piston_groove (groove dia, male gland, +0/-.002), A1_rod_groove (groove dia, female gland), B_rod (tube/rod OD, female gland, +0/-.002), C_plug (plug OD, male gland, +0/-.001), D_throat (throat dia, female gland, +.001/-0); 1500 psi static, no back-up ring
columns.parker_t42_note: present only where Parker flags considerable installation stretch for the male gland, or where the Table 4-2 transcription failed the row arithmetic (A - B1 = A1 - B = 2F, A - C = D - B = E) and was corrected or kept as noted
columns.confidence: certain | likely | recall - applies to id_in and id_tol_in; nothing is "certain" because no value was read from the SAE standard itself in this session (see license_note)
columns.source: standard and cross-check documents the values come from
columns.disputed: present only where the reviewers or the two tolerance sources disagreed: {field, alternatives:[{value, source}], note}
columns.note: present only on rows changed at reconciliation

gland_parker_ord5700.how_to_read: Inch values are as the Parker handbook prints them; mm are x25.4 rounded to 2 decimals. Face seals (axial squeeze, e.g. av-bay bulkhead against a coupler shoulder, tank end cap flange) use face_seal_chart_4_3. Radial piston/rod seals (e.g. an end cap plug sliding into a tank bore) use radial_static_table_4_2 together with the per-row parker_t42_* diameters: piston seal -> bore A, groove bottom B1, plug OD C; rod/female seal -> groove A1, rod B, throat D. Gland depth for a radial seal INCLUDES the diametral clearance E: L = (A - B1)/2.

usage_formulas.face_seal_pressure_outside (av-bay bulkh: groove ID = O-ring id (pick the dash whose id is at or just under the groove ID); groove OD = groove ID + 2 x G; depth = L from Chart 4-3
usage_formulas.face_seal_pressure_inside (tank end cap: groove OD = O-ring od_in/od_mm (pick the dash whose OD is at or just over the groove OD); groove ID = groove OD - 2 x G
usage_formulas.radial_piston_seal: use the per-row parker_t42 values directly: bore = A, groove bottom = B1 (+0/-.002 in), plug OD = C (+0/-.001 in), groove width = G (+.005/-0); or generically bore = id + 2 x cs (nominal, no stretch) and groove bottom = bore - 2 x L
usage_formulas.radial_rod_seal: groove dia = A1, rod = B, throat = D from the per-row parker_t42 values
usage_formulas.fill: groove fill = (pi/4 x cs^2) / (depth x width) at max cs and min groove; keep <= ~90 % for liquids, <= ~95 % for vacuum/gases with the narrower groove; the id_tol_in column is what makes the worst-case stretch and fill computable
usage_formulas.stretch: Parker: every 3 % of ID stretch reduces W by about 1 %; keep piston-seal stretch to 1-5 %, never more than ~5 % on W .103 (PartForge doctrine, not Parker)
usage_formulas.confidence: likely (Parker ORD 5700 sections 3-4 practice; the formulas are arithmetic on cited fields)

table_4_2_rating.value: Design Table 4-2 is headed for industrial static seals to 103.5 bar (1500 psi), and its footnote says the tabulated groove width G does not permit back-up rings and that back-up rings are to be used above 103.5 bar. This is a table heading and an investigation trigger, not a certification: capability depends on the total OPERATING diametral clearance (bore dilation and bolt stretch under pressure included), compound hardness, temperature and whether pressure is steady, pulsating or vibrating. Silicone and fluorosilicone: halve the maximum diametral clearance (Table 4-2 note).
table_4_2_rating.source: Parker ORD 5700 Table 4-2 title and footnotes as transcribed in KasperCalc ORing-HighPressureIndustrial.html and reported independently at manuals.plus; the 'investigate back-ups above 103.5 bar' trigger also reported from Parker O-Ring Division FAQ.pdf. The printed handbook was not read.

tank_end_cap_case.value: A 60 bar (870 psi) N2O tank end cap, 70 A NBR or FKM, W .139, radial piston seal held to Table 4-2 clearance E .003-.006 in total diametral (0.08-0.15 mm) is inside the 1500 psi Table 4-2 envelope with ~1.7x margin and needs no back-up ring; if the bore/plug clearance is opened to 0.10 mm diametral (endcap.scad) it is still within E max .006 in = 0.15 mm
tank_end_cap_case.source: arithmetic on the Table 4-2 rating above

figure_3_2_extrusion_limits.value: Parker Figure 3-2 (basis 100,000 pressure cycles at 71 C, total diametral clearance): 70 Shore A roughly .010 in at ~800 psi, .005 in at ~1500 psi, .002 in at ~3000 psi; 80 A roughly .010 in at ~1500 psi, .005 in at ~3000 psi; 90 A roughly .010 in at ~3000 psi, .005 in at ~5000 psi. Above the curve add one back-up ring (width G1) on the low-pressure side, two (G2) if pressure alternates direction, or step up to 90 A.
figure_3_2_extrusion_limits.source: Parker ORD 5700 Figure 3-2, from memory; read the printed curve before relying on any single point

backup_rings_above_103_5_bar.value: above 103.5 bar (1500 psi) Table 4-2's groove does not apply: use back-up rings with the wider groove (G1 one ring on the low-pressure side, G2 two rings if pressure alternates direction)
backup_rings_above_103_5_bar.source: Parker ORD 5700 Table 4-2 footnote (two transcriptions) and Parker O-Ring Division FAQ (reported)

figure_3_2_check_above_55_2_bar.value: above 55.2 bar (800 psi) Parker refers the designer to Figure 3-2: hold the total operating diametral clearance for the chosen durometer inside the curve, or step up to 90 A, or add a back-up ring - the fix for a gap that is too wide is hardness or a back-up, not a heavier cross-section
figure_3_2_check_above_55_2_bar.source: A Parker Table 4-2 extract reported (via search summary, not read) to refer the designer to Figure 3-2 above 800 psi; the 800 psi figure is single-source

bore_lead_in_chamfer.value: 15-20 deg chamfer on the bore (or the plug) over a length at least equal to the O-ring cross-section, edges polished; the groove edges broken with the R radius, never sharp
bore_lead_in_chamfer.source: Parker ORD 5700 section 4 (static seal design), from memory

surface_finish.value: Sealing surfaces (bore, plug OD, face-seal land) 16 uin Ra (0.4 um) for vacuum and gases, 32 uin Ra (0.8 um) for liquids; groove sides and bottom 63 uin Ra (1.6 um); no lead, spiral or circumferential scratches across the seal
surface_finish.source: Parker ORD 5700 Table 3-x surface-finish recommendations, from memory

groove_bottom_tolerance.value: Groove diameter B1 (piston) +0/-.002 in (0 / -0.05 mm); bore A +.002/-0; groove width G +.005/-0 (0 / +0.13 mm); so the drawing tolerance on a piston groove bottom is -0.05 mm, tighter than the +/-0.05 mm the endcap.scad fixture carries
groove_bottom_tolerance.source: Parker ORD 5700 Table 4-2 tolerance columns as transcribed in KasperCalc

media_guidance_rocketry.value: NBR (70 A) for ejection-charge pressure, air, water, hydrocarbon fuels; FKM (Viton, 75-90 A) where hot ejection gas (100-200 C short exposure) or oxidiser vapour is present; silicone is gas-permeable and low-strength, use only for low-pressure face seals; N2O attacks many elastomers by swelling and is an oxidiser under adiabatic compression, so a nitrous tank seal must be chosen from the supplier's N2O compatibility chart (FKM or PTFE-encapsulated FKM are the usual answers, NBR is often listed as acceptable for N2O but is not for LOX or high-concentration H2O2) and lubricated only with an oxidiser-compatible fluorinated grease; never PTFE tape shreds or hydrocarbon grease on an oxidiser boundary
media_guidance_rocketry.source: Parker ORD 5700 section 2 (compound selection) and general vendor compatibility charts, from memory; not a substitute for the supplier chart

selection_practice_partforge_doctrine.value: PartForge shop practice, NOT Parker: W .103 (2.62 mm) for couplers and bulkheads under 2 bar; W .139 (3.53 mm) as the default for any pressure-vessel end cap or radial seal at 2 bar and above, at every bore the table covers. Step up to W .210 (5.33 mm) only when the shop cannot hold the groove-bottom tolerance Table 4-2 asks for (B1 +0/-.002 in), the sealing face is rough or reused, or the ring is hand-assembled repeatedly in the field - tolerance and handling reasons, never because the bore is large and never because the pressure is high. Hobby vendors stock -1xx and -2xx up to about -284; 3xx above -360 and all 4xx are special order.
selection_practice_partforge_doctrine.source: PartForge shop doctrine (sport-rocketry practice); do not cite Parker for these thresholds. The earlier form of this note ("W .210 for anything above 75 mm bore under real pressure") was withdrawn on 2026-09-20: see cross_section_facts and reconciliation.later_passes.

w_070_family.value: AS568 -004..-050 (W .070 in / 1.78 mm, ID .070 to 5.239 in) exist and are what the PartForge doctrine 1.78 mm face-seal figures refer to (feedthroughs, charge wells, vent ports). Out of this table's scope: 45 sizes, plus the odd -001..-003 (W .040/.050/.060). Face and radial gland values for W .070 ARE included above.
w_070_family.source: Apple Rubber AS568 chart and KasperCalc AS568D table (both list -001..-050)

cross_section_facts.value: Parker ORD 5700 gives NO rule for choosing a cross-section from bore size or pressure: Tables 4-1/4-2/4-3 are entered with W already chosen and tabulate the gland for each W. In this table's own rows every W spans nearly the whole diameter range - W .103 to -178 (9.737 in ID), W .139 to -284 (17.955 in ID), W .210 from -309 (0.412 in ID) - and only the -4xx family (W .275) has a large-diameter floor, at -425 (4.475 in ID). Table 4-2 allows the SAME diametral clearance E, .003-.006 in (0.08-0.15 mm), for W .139 and W .210 (radial_static_table_4_2), so stepping from a -2xx to a -3xx on the same bore buys no extrusion margin; only W .275 gains .001 in. What a heavier section buys is absolute squeeze - squeeze is a percentage of W - i.e. tolerance to groove-depth error, flatness, scratches and debris, and easier handling; three vendor design guides were reported to agree on that (Gallagher Seals, Global O-Ring, Hi-Tech Seals) but none was read in this project, so that last clause is recall.
cross_section_facts.source: The ID coverage and the identical E band are read from this table's reconciled rows and its radial_static_table_4_2 bands (three transcriptions agree); the absence of a selection rule is the structure of Parker's tables (KasperCalc transcription of Table 4-2 and Chart 4-3; the printed handbook was not read). The vendor-guide clause is recall.
